items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Well I played some with a little band, with Bernie Young, Al Simeon, Omar Simeon, Jimmy McHenry, and people like that, you know.

ctx.x: But anyway, so you started taking lessons when you were about 18 years old. And then when did you start playing music?

Well then, I'll tell you what happened. I've forgotten about this. I returned in the Orleans in 1921. That's when I met Chester's artists. They were advertising. And I rode on the truck. While I'm still in the preliminary stages. So. You hadn't played any jobs yet. Well I played some with a little band, with Bernie Young, Al Simeon, Omar Simeon, Jimmy McHenry, and people like that, you know. And we were non-union. Just 15? Yeah, we were non-union then. items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: And the fellas who later became the Simeon boys' brother-in-law by the name of Warden played piano. So Bernie got these fellas together and we formed a little band.

ctx.x: So when was the first music that you were interested in? Did you start on the trombone or which instrument did you start on?

Well, my first instrument was trombone, but it wasn't my favorite instrument. I'd like to tell you, Bill, about how I come to study the trombone. While talking with Joe Oliver, it must have been somewhere around 1920, 1921, somewhere along there. He, I told Joe Oliver that I was going to take lessons on the trombone.
